claims.text: Sprint 14's backlog in docs/team/sprint-example.md has an Ước lượng column: 3 (cancel endpoint), 3 (cancel button), 2 (block cancelling a paid order), 2 (stop notifications for cancelled orders), 1 (wrong total bug); they add up to 11.
The 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy' item (estimate 2) did not finish and moved to the next sprint; the sprint review did not demonstrate it because unfinished work does not count.

Teams estimate to plan how much fits in a sprint or roughly how long larger work takes; estimates are made with information available before the work and are sometimes wrong in both directions; they are a planning tool, not a promise.
A Kanban team that limits work in progress instead of planning a batch has less need to size each item in advance.

claims.text: When estimates are treated as deadlines, people tend to give larger numbers to protect themselves, and the numbers stop helping planning.
Sprint 14's estimates are relative sizes (the retrospective speaks of items larger than 3 points), not hours or days.
